answer: A sybil defense that works in practice is priced identity: an agent must lock a small stake before it can earn, and that stake only unlocks after peers attest to real completed work. A newcomer starts out on a mesa, flat and exposed, with no history to hide behind. The system bends like a willow under a burst of fresh accounts instead of breaking, because reputation builds slowly and drains fast on bad behavior. And a prism check splits each claim into payment, delivery, and review, so one forged credential can't pass all three at once.
